The pages opened do not mention a 1743 cession. After 1697 the Mataram page has Blambangan 'rejoined Bali ... after the Mataram troops withdrew' and the Banyuwangi page 'around 150 years of Balinese occupation'; the Balinese suzerainty belongs on the Bali dossier.

1635: Mataram's war on the Hindu kingdom begins. Infobox 'Blambangan became the vassal of Mataram Sultanate aftermath of the war: 1635-1639'; Sultan Agung 'launched a holy war against the still-Hindu Blambangan' (Mataram page, undated).

1639: Blambangan surrenders to Mataram. 'the conquest of Blambangan by the forces of Sultan Agung of Mataram took place in 1639'; 'Blambangan surrendered in 1639, but quickly regained their independence in 1659' (Mataram page). The vassal tint 1639-1659 belongs to the Mataram dossier.

1665: Tawang Alun II founds Macan Putih near Banyuwangi. 'In 1665, Tawang Alun II Danureja, the 8th king of Blambangan, opened the forest of Sudiamara' (Blambangan page); he 'freed Blambangan from Mataram during the Trunajaya revolt' (Banyuwangi page). His territory 'reached Jember, Lumajang, Situbondo, and Bali'.

1768: Blambangan passes to the Dutch. Infobox 'Absorbed into the territory of Dutch East Indies: 1768/1777'; Wong Agung Wilis ruled 1767-1768. The page gives no war or treaty; the Banyuwangi page has it VOC-controlled by 1770.
1768: the Hindu kingdom of Blambangan ends under the Dutch East India Company (infobox 1768/1777).

notes: Cliopatria 'Blambangan Kingdom' (4 shapes, 1519..1743). (1) The 1519 shape (27,732 km2) reaches west to the Surabaya-Mojokerto country; the page has the kingdom east of Surabaya, and Cliopatria's own 1619 step drops 52 cells. The dossier corrects to the eastern salient (the 1741 outline, 13,815 km2) with Pasuruan and Pajarakan until their loss to Demak in 1545-1546. (2) Start: the page's infobox puts independence in 1478 (Mas Sembar, Semboro); Cliopatria begins in 1519 and the Majapahit dossier (se-02-c) keeps all of East Java in Majapahit to 1518, so the new 1478-1518 keyframe overlaps Majapahit's shape; the reviewer or colour agent must decide (the cells are Majapahit's if 1518 stands, Blambangan's if the Blambangan infobox does). (3) End: Cliopatria 1743 is unsupported by the pages opened (nothing on a 1743 cession); the infobox says 1768/1777, and 1768 is used. (4) Vassalage on both sides is for the suzerains' dossiers: Mataram 1639-1659 (vassal 1635-1639 on the Blambangan page, 1639 surrender and 1659 independence on the Mataram page) and Bali after 1697; the 'Pasuruan army had taken Blambangan some years ago' (Dutch report of early 1601) is undated and not drawn. (5) The Banyuwangi page's 'around 150 years of Balinese occupation' and the Mataram page's 'rejoined Bali in 1697' disagree with the infobox's Blambangan independence under Tawang Alun II (1665-1691); the Bali dossier ('bali', 1687-1907, another batch) should carry the Balinese suzerainty. (6) Capitals: coordinates are the researcher's approximations; years for Panarukan (1527-1600) and Muncar (1692-1762) are bridged from the infobox's ruler periods; Kedawung and Lateng are omitted because the page gives no years or places. (7) The fetch tool returns a model summary of each page; quotation marks mean 'as the fetched text gave it'. Counterparts needing dossiers: none new (demak-sultanate, mataram-sultanate, majapahit, balinese-kingdom, dutch-east-indies exist or are being written); Pasuruan as a state is not given a dossier.
